instruction: Move the text layer downward to position it near the bottom of the image.

metadata.explanation: Task requires moving the text layer downward. Evaluator checks if the bottommost dark pixel is within the bottom 5% of the image height. Verified: Text layer can be moved vertically to bottom edge.

llm_judge_reasons: Evaluator correctly verifies the instruction requirement: text layer positioned near bottom of image
Metric logic at gimp.py:27-43 is sound: scans from bottom to top to find bottommost row containing any dark pixel (grayscale < 128)
The break statement at line 34 is CORRECT - it exits the inner loop after confirming the current row contains a dark pixel, which is sufficient to identify this row as containing text
Previous judge's concern about 'only checking left side' is incorrect - the algorithm only needs to know IF a row has dark pixels, not WHERE in the row they are located
Orange background (from orange_background.xcf) has grayscale value > 128, so won't trigger false positives for dark pixel detection
Postconfig appropriately exports the image to PNG for verification of final state
Returns 1.0 if bottommost dark pixel is in bottom 5% of image height (y > height * 0.95), which semantically matches 'near the bottom'
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Minor: Consider if 5% threshold is appropriate for all image sizes - might want to make this configurable or use absolute pixel distance
Minor: Could add validation to ensure at least some dark pixels exist (bottom_most_dark_pixel > 0) to avoid false positives on empty/all-light images
Minor: Consider adding metadata about what constitutes 'near the bottom' (currently hardcoded 5%) for transparency
